4.text: The principal hunting-ceremonial is celebrated at the conclusion of the hunt.

5.text: During the ceremony the carcasses are kept behind the tent on the snow.

6.text: The carcass must be butchered on the spot where it lies. The hams and

7.text: shoulders may be taken for consumption. The head, back, and pelvis must

8.text: be left with the skin on and uncut; and the heart and the aorta must also

9.text: be left intact. The heads must be covered for the night, and uncovered in

10.text: the morning. The fire-boards are kept with the carcass during the night,

12.text: On the morning of the ceremonial two reindeer are slaughtered, — one

13.text: as a sacrifice to the reindeer-bucks killed, and the other to the dawn. Some-

14.text: times a third reindeer is sacrificed to the nadir. The antlers of the wild bucks

15.text: are adorned with festoons of sausages and dried guts. Blood-soup, meat-soup,

16.text: and meat are cooked in abundance. The meal and the feeding of the charms

17.text: proceed as usual. Then a female fawn is slaughtered, and the antlers painted

21.text: heads are kept for the family, and taken into the tent, where they are
